meta.title: Primes never run out
meta.subtitle: Euclid's proof in under a minute
meta.attribution: Proof: Euclid, Elements, Book IX, Proposition 20

lines.caption: Primes are the whole numbers you can't split into smaller factors.
Do they ever run out? About 2,300 years ago, Euclid showed they don't.
Suppose you had a complete list of primes, say two, three and five.
Multiply them together and add one. You get thirty-one.
Dividing it by any prime on the list leaves a remainder of one, so its prime factors are all new.
Any finite list is missing a prime. So the list never ends.
